us.title: Super Mario 3D Land Dared To Embrace 2D Mario In A 3D World
us.description: Super Mario 3D Land is celebrating its 15-year anniversary today, November 13, 2026. Below, we examine how 3D Land was a true iteration of the classic 2D Mario formula. I remember when the first preview images of Super Mario 64 began circulating in gaming magazines. The thought of playing a Mario game in THREE DEEEEEE blew my tiny 8-year-old mind. While the final game was absolutely wonderful, it wasn’t quite what I had in my head when I thought about Mario gameplay translated into three dimensions. The worlds were vast and open-ended. Instead of running and jumping toward the goal, players had missions to accomplish. Puzzles to solve. Specific enemies to beat. Trinkets to find. Mario had a life bar. An air meter when underwater. Power-ups were temporary, vanishing after a certain time had elapsed. And don’t get me wrong. It was different from what I imagined, but it worked. All of it worked. Nintendo had a winning formula on its hands, one that 3D Mario games would carry forward with Super Mario Sunshine and, to a lesser extent, the Super Mario Galaxy duology. But deep down, I couldn’t help but wonder what it would have been like in some alternate universe where they had adhered to the classic Mario formula instead in the move to 3D. Thankfully, I didn’t have to wonder forever, because in 2011, Super Mario 3D Land released for the 3DS and changed what a 3D Mario game could be. How? By doing exactly what I wanted Super Mario 64 to do 15 years prior: fully translate the classic 2D Mario style and gameplay to the third dimension. Even looking at 3D Land’s cover art evokes memories of the plumber’s colorful side-scrolling escapades. We see Mario hopping around a colorful environment full to the brim with blocks, pipes, platforms, even classic power-ups like the Fire Flower tucked away in the corner. And few elements could get the nostalgia juices flowing like the inclusion of the iconic Super Leaf from Super Mario Bros. 3. The game promised to be something different yet comfortingly familiar. And what’s more comfortingly familiar than Bowser capturing Princess Peach and Mario racing off to rescue her? But even the simplest of Mario plots has to have at least one wrinkle. Due to a storm the night before, the land has been coated in Super Leaves, and now, Bowser and many of his minions have access to raccoon tails and the power of limited flight, just as Mario does. Yes, the Super Leaf is the real star of the show here, marking the power-up’s first appearance in over two decades. You’d be hard-pressed to go through a level without either running into one of the raccoon power-ups or seeing one of Bowser’s minions imbued with it. Even the notoriously heavy Thwomps gracefully float about in the air as if they were light as feathers. 3D Land drills the point home that power-ups are back in a big way, no longer relegated to temporary usage as was the case with previous 3D titles. Joining the Tanooki Suit is the ever-classic Super Mushroom, allowing Mario to take an extra hit before dying—no life bar here!—and the aforementioned Fire Flower. New to the game is the Boomerang Suit, a spiritual successor to Super Mario Bros. 3’s Hammer Suit that can take out enemies coming and going (because it’s a boomerang, you see). Skilled players can go from level to level, even world to world, without ever losing the utility of a power-up at their disposal. The power-ups wouldn’t be nearly as fun without great levels to use them in. 3D Land foregoes sprawling sandboxes for the more linear, self-contained, obstacle-course-like levels that first made Mario famous: Hop across colorful floating platforms, bonk some enemies, and slide down the flagpole at the end in classic Mario fashion. And at the end of each world, you take on Bowser (or at least a reasonable facsimile) on a bridge in a 3D variation of the classic boss fights from the original Super Mario Bros. This made 3D Land the perfect portable Mario game for bursts of quick fun on the go. It was 3D Mario in the palm of your hand when the Switch was still just a twinkle in Nintendo’s eye. So, was this refreshing take on 3D Mario met with a warm reception from fans? Well, yeah, but not as much as I would have hoped. Many fans decried 3D Land for deviating from the sandbox and exploratory gameplay the 3D games had showcased up to that point. To them, it felt “safe,” unwilling to take the big risks of its 3D predecessors. To which I argue…what’s wrong with that? Despite being a smaller and more conservative Mario adventure, it did exactly what it sought out to do: make the classic 2D Mario experience the foundation of a 3D Mario game for the first time. Even if it didn’t take any huge swings, the novelty of the concept is more than enough to make the game a classic in my eyes. And the fact that the game would pave the way for the fantastic Super Mario 3D World a few years later further demonstrates that the concept had legs. Super Mario 3D Land deserves to be judged on what it is, not what it isn’t. It was pure, distilled, classic 2D Mario on a three-dimensional plane, and I’ll remember it fondly for another 15 years.

fr.title: Grégory Ascher et Justine Salmon de RTL 2 ont réveillé les Aubois avec leur Double Expresso
fr.description: Lecture zen Les Aubois se sont levés aux aurores vendredi 13 novembre pour assister à la matinale de RTL 2 Le Double Expresso, animée par Justine Salmon et Grégory Ascher. Les portes n’avaient pas encore ouvert que déjà ils faisaient la queue devant la Chapelle Argence Troyes. 300 personnes, qui s’étaient inscrites préalablement, ont ainsi pu participer à l’émission de radio délocalisée pour la première fois à Troyes, diffusée sur W9. « On est hyper content d’être là » Alors que l’équipe est à pied d’œuvre, les présentateurs déjà présents sur la scène montrent déjà toute la complicité qui les unit. Dix ans et demi à œuvrer en binôme, cela ne s’improvise pas. Il faut une dose de bonne humeur et de sympathie pour tout donner en direct pendant trois heures. « Mon objectif, c’est de gêner toute la matinée. Il y a du public, c’est pour ça que je fais le cabot. J’ai une énorme passion pour le malaise », plaisante Greg Ascher. Il s’est fait plaisir. Comme un running gag, il a demandé à l’envi si « un Double expresso à Troyes, ça fait six ». Ils sont arrivés à Troyes jeudi et ont pris le temps de découvrir la ville, les commerçants pour apprendre à découvrir et à connaître Troyes. Pendant les pauses musicales ou les pubs, l’ambiance se veut détendue. On blague, on échange, on interpelle les spectateurs. Greg Ascher vient même s’asseoir au milieu de l’assistance. À l’aise et très accessible, Greg et Justine font le show. « C’est génial. Le public est hyper chaud. On est hyper content d’être là », confient-ils pendant une coupure pub. « On s’amuse beaucoup, nos intervenants sont très à l’aise et le public enthousiaste. » Jenn Ayache sur scène Sur scène, se succèdent Aurélie Puy, directrice de l’agence Prêt à Partir, pour parler de son nouveau concept de voyage mystère, Yvon Georges, président du Suma, pour évoquer le motoball, Franck Poncelet et Maïté Vinclair, de la Maison du Boulanger, mais aussi Patrick Maury. Notre champion du monde de l’andouillette a fait forte impression, offrant une dégustation au petit matin à l’équipe mais aussi au public. Un petit déj café andouillette que les Ch’tis pourraient presque nous envier. « Son andouillette est d’une qualité extraordinaire. C’est vraiment du très haut niveau », se régale Greg Ascher alors que Justine est plus mitigée sur le sujet. « C’est une grande première. Je n’en avais jamais goûté. C’est particulier mais j’ai senti qu’elle était très bonne. » Bien sûr, Le Double Expresso était là pour parler de Troyes mais aussi de musique avec une invitée de marque, la chanteuse Jenn Ayache, venue interpréter deux titres en live, Lola et la reprise About Us de Tattoo. Un avant-goût de ce qui attend les Aubois le 18 décembre prochain, puisque l’artiste sera en concert au Cube, dans le cadre des Nuits en +, avec son groupe Superbus. Trois heures d’émission, dans la bonne humeur et la convivialité, qui sont passées à toute vitesse. Mais une fois les caméras et les micros éteints, en toute simplicité, Greg et Justine ont continué à jouer le jeu, prenant le temps d’échanger avec leurs auditeurs et de faire une photo souvenir. Mis en ligne le 13/11/2026 à 20:04 Grégory Ascher et Justine Salmon de RTL 2 ont réveillé les Aubois avec leur Double Expresso C’était leur première délocalisation à Troyes et ils s’en souviendront. Grégory Ascher et Justine Salmon ont posé vendredi matin leurs valises pour la matinale de RTL 2 « Le Double Expresso » devant un public conquis par leur naturel et leur accessibilité.

Cuestionada sobre la información relacionada con un posible desbloqueo de cuentas y si esto podría representar una exoneración de Rocha Moya, la Gobernadora evitó emitir una postura y señaló que corresponde a las autoridades responsables informar sobre sus determinaciones. “Desconozco, hay que preguntarle”, respondió. También negó haber conversado con el Gobernador sobre el tema. “No, no hablamos de estos temas, somos muy respetuosos de las instancias que están haciendo su trabajo y la UIF no tiene que rendirle cuentas a los gobiernos de los estados”, declaró. Domínguez Nava sostuvo que la Unidad de Inteligencia Financiera es la instancia encargada de generar y comunicar la información correspondiente, de acuerdo con sus atribuciones. Añadió que las autoridades federales hacen pública la información cuando así lo consideran pertinente y bajo los principios de transparencia. La Mandataria estatal insistió en que su Gobierno no interviene en las decisiones de las instituciones encargadas de investigar estos asuntos.

in.title: O.M Trailer Out: Dhanush's Operation Mole against red sandalwood mafia looks intense, Mammootty & Sai Pallavi steal show
in.description: After much delay, the much-awaited trailer for Dhanush's O.M i.e., OPERATION MOLE Chapter 1: Udhiram - The Blood Wood, is finally out, and it lives up to the hype. The trailer introduces us to the world of red sandalwood smuggling. Dhanush plays a woodcutter who gets pulled deep into the dangerous syndicate. O.M i.e., OPERATION MOLE Sai Pallavi, who is currently winning hearts as Sita Mata in Ramayana, makes a powerful impact as Nithya Reddy, a CBI officer in O.M. Her character glimpse earlier described her as a mix of "honesty, smartness, and experience in young blood," and the trailer shows her leading Operation Mole to bust the smuggling ring. The biggest surprise is Mammootty, who seems to be playing a politician. In his first on-screen collaboration with Dhanush, he appears in a grey-shaded, commanding avatar who seems to control the trade from the shadows. The trailer also gives a glimpse of Naseeruddin Shah. Though his character details remain under wraps, it seems to be a short role. Besides the four acting giants, Sreeleela also stars in the film. She is playing Dhanush's wife. Her look is very realistic and natural. The film is written and directed by Rajkumar Periasamy of Amaran fame, with music by Sai Abhyankar. Produced by Wunderbar Films and RTake Studios, the film is mounted as a franchise opener. With slick action, strong performances, and a gripping story, O.M looks like a promising bet from Tamil Cinema this year. The project is planned as the first instalment of a two-part franchise. Initially scheduled for an October release, the film was postponed to avoid a box-office clash with Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 and Suriya's Scene. The film hits theatres worldwide on November 20, 2026. id.title: PAN Banyumas Tegaskan Tegak Lurus, Dukung Penuh Kepemimpinan Zulkifli Hasan
id.description: BANYUMAS, parahyangan-post.com- – Dewan Pimpinan Daerah (DPD) Partai Amanat Nasional (PAN) Kabupaten Banyumas menegaskan sikap tegak lurus dan dukungan penuh terhadap Zulkifli Hasan sebagai Ketua Umum DPP PAN. Seluruh jajaran kepengurusan PAN Banyumas menyatakan tetap berada dalam satu barisan dan satu komando di bawah kepemimpinan Zulkifli Hasan. Penegasan ini sekaligus menunjukkan soliditas organisasi dalam menjaga arah perjuangan partai hingga tingkat akar rumput. Ketua DPD PAN Banyumas, Akhmad Saiful Hadi, S.Hut., menegaskan bahwa dukungan terhadap Zulkifli Hasan merupakan sikap politik organisasi yang harus dijaga oleh seluruh kader. Menurutnya, kepemimpinan Zulkifli Hasan menjadi bagian penting dalam menjaga kesinambungan arah perjuangan PAN secara nasional maupun di daerah. “PAN Banyumas memiliki sikap yang jelas. Kami mendukung penuh kepemimpinan Zulkifli Hasan sebagai Ketua Umum DPP PAN. Seluruh jajaran harus menjaga soliditas, menghormati garis kebijakan partai, dan tetap bergerak dalam satu komando. Bagi kami, yang terpenting adalah bagaimana PAN terus tumbuh, semakin kuat, dan hadir memberikan manfaat bagi masyarakat,” tegas Akhmad Saiful Hadi. Ia juga mengingatkan bahwa kekuatan partai sangat bergantung pada kesatuan sikap dan komitmen seluruh kader dalam menjalankan perjuangan organisasi. Karena itu, dukungan terhadap kepemimpinan Ketua Umum harus tercermin dalam kerja nyata, kedisiplinan kader, serta kesungguhan membangun PAN di wilayah masing-masing. Senada dengan hal tersebut, Sekretaris DPD PAN Banyumas, Cipto Pujiharso, S.E., M.M., menyampaikan bahwa seluruh jajaran PAN di Kabupaten Banyumas tetap solid dan memiliki kesamaan sikap dalam mendukung Zulkifli Hasan. Soliditas tersebut terus diperkuat melalui konsolidasi organisasi yang berjalan secara berjenjang, mulai dari DPD, DPC hingga DPRT di seluruh wilayah Kabupaten Banyumas. “Bagi kami, sikapnya jelas. PAN Banyumas tegak lurus dan mendukung penuh Zulkifli Hasan sebagai Ketua Umum DPP PAN. Seluruh jajaran tetap satu komando, satu barisan, dan satu arah dalam menjalankan perjuangan partai,” tegas Cipto Pujiharso, S.E., M.M. Menurutnya, konsolidasi menjadi bagian penting untuk memastikan komunikasi dan koordinasi antartingkatan kepengurusan tetap terjaga. Melalui penguatan struktur organisasi, seluruh kader diharapkan memiliki pemahaman yang sama terhadap arah perjuangan partai serta mampu menjalankan agenda organisasi secara konsisten. Cipto menambahkan, soliditas organisasi harus diwujudkan melalui kekompakan kader dan keberpihakan terhadap kepentingan masyarakat. Ia mengajak seluruh jajaran PAN Banyumas untuk tidak kehilangan fokus dalam menjalankan kerja-kerja politik dan sosial, sekaligus terus memperkuat kehadiran partai di tengah masyarakat. Dukungan terhadap kepemimpinan Zulkifli Hasan, lanjutnya, harus menjadi energi bersama untuk membesarkan PAN dan memperkuat kepercayaan masyarakat. Dengan konsolidasi yang terus berjalan serta komunikasi yang terjaga hingga tingkat ranting, PAN Banyumas berkomitmen mempertahankan soliditas dan menjalankan perjuangan organisasi dalam satu arah. “Seluruh kader PAN Banyumas harus tetap solid dan menjaga semangat kebersamaan. Kami tegak lurus bersama Zulkifli Hasan. Dukungan ini menjadi sikap dan komitmen seluruh jajaran untuk terus membesarkan PAN serta memperjuangkan kepentingan masyarakat,” pungkas Cipto Pujiharso, S.E., M.M.

bd.title: Cuisine. K Wraps Up K-Seafood Culinary Program in Seattle
bd.description: Co-hosted with the Korea Fisheries Association, the hands-on program introduced South Seattle College students, local consumers and content creators to the ingredients, techniques and everyday versatility of Korean seafood. SEATTLE, Nov. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CJ Foods' Korean cuisine talent discovery and development platform, Cuisine.K, successfully hosted a K-Seafood Cooking Class in Seattle. Co-hosted by CJ Foods and the Korea Fisheries Association, the program aimed to expand awareness and hands-on appreciation of Korean seafood ingredients and dishes among students, local consumers and content creators. Participants, judges, and Cuisine. K representatives at the K-Seafood Cooking Contest The program was held from November 5 to 7 at South Seattle College (SSC). A K-Seafood cooking competition for SSC students took place on November 5, followed by a cooking class for SSC students on November 6. On November 7, Cuisine. K hosted two hands-on cooking class sessions for local consumers and content creators. Chef Yeon-ju Lee, a Cuisine. K alumna, owner chef of JULIEAT Catering and a contestant on Netflix's Culinary Class Wars Season 1, participated as the lead chef. Together with other Cuisine. K alumni chefs, Chef Lee introduced participants to Korean seafood ingredients including oysters, gim (seaweed) and anchovies. During the November 6 session for SSC students, the chefs demonstrated Soy-Braised Oyster Rice Bowl and Gim Pancake dishes, showcasing creative and approachable ways to incorporate oysters into contemporary cuisine. Through the demonstration, students gained a deeper understanding of Korean seafood ingredients and explored their potential across a range of fine dining culinary applications. On November 7, the chefs led hands-on cooking classes for local consumers and content creators. Participants learned to prepare Oyster Mini Gimbap and Oyster Sandwich, experiencing firsthand how Korean seafood ingredients can be incorporated into everyday meals. The program highlighted the versatility of Korean oysters and gim while offering participants practical cooking techniques they can recreate at home. Prior to the cooking classes, SSC students participated in a K-Seafood cooking competition on November 5. Chef Lee served as a judge as students presented their own original Korean dishes featuring K-Seafood ingredients. Team Seoul Sisters (Foziya Robale, Deeqa Yusuf, and Shreya Pradhan) took first place with its anchovy seaweed pasta, oyster bulgogi sambusa, and black sesame macaron. "It was a meaningful opportunity to introduce the diverse appeal of Korean seafood to students and local consumers in Seattle in collaboration with the Korea Fisheries Association," said Sangmyeong Kim, Project Manager of the Hansik 245 Team at CJ Foods. "Through Cuisine.K, we will continue to discover and nurture Korean culinary talent while creating opportunities for consumers around the world to experience and enjoy K-food culture as part of their everyday lives." Cuisine. K is CJ Foods' platform for discovering, developing and connecting Korean culinary talent with audiences around the world. Moving beyond simply raising awareness of K-food, the initiative focuses on helping global consumers experience Korean cuisine in practical and repeatable ways through chef-led cooking classes, pop-ups, competitions and other interactive programs. By supporting chefs at different stages of their careers and enabling them to communicate the flavors, techniques and cultural context of Korean cuisine, Cuisine. K aims to help K-food evolve from a cultural trend into an everyday choice for consumers worldwide. The Korea Fisheries Association (KFA), an implementing organization for the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries' Overseas Market Development Program for Korean Seafood, has been actively promoting Korean seafood products in global markets through various marketing initiatives aimed at raising awareness and expanding consumer demand. As part of these efforts, the program featured hands-on cooking classes for local culinary students and consumers, highlighting the quality of Korean seafood while introducing diverse cooking techniques and practical ways to incorporate Korean seafood ingredients into everyday meals. About CJ Foods CJ Foods, a business unit of CJ CheilJedang, is a global food company delivering a variety of products ranging from food ingredients and frozen/chilled foods to appetizers. Established as Korea's first sugar manufacturer in 1953, CJ Foods has grown to become the country's largest food company. Today, it is leading the global food industry with its renowned Korean food brand, bibigo™. In the U.S., CJ Foods operates its business through CJ Schwan's, a U.S.-based affiliate, running 20 production facilities across the country. The company operates in multiple regions worldwide including South Korea, the U.S. (as CJ Schwan's), Japan, China, Southeast Asia, Europe, and Oceania. For more information, visit https://www.cj.co.kr/en/aboutus/business/lifestyle-foods About the Korea Fisheries Association The Korea Fisheries Association (KFA) is an organization dedicated to supporting the development of Korea's fisheries sector and strengthening the competitiveness of its seafood industry. As an implementing organization for the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries' Overseas Market Development Program for Korean Seafood, KFA works to raise global awareness of Korean seafood products and expand export opportunities through international promotional and marketing initiatives, support for seafood exporters, and hands-on consumer experience programs in overseas markets. bd.title: 55-Foot Christmas Tree Lights Up Toronto as The Distillery Winter Village, presented by Quince, Opens for 2026
bd.description: Toronto's world-famous Christmas market returns with new attractions, special performances and holiday experiences through January 3, 2027 TORONTO, Nov. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Distillery Winter Village, presented by Quince, officially opened its 2026 season on November 12 with the lighting of its iconic 16.8-metre (55-foot) Christmas tree. Thousands gathered in Toronto's Distillery Historic District to join Santa in the countdown as the towering silver fir, adorned with more than 80,000 white lights and hundreds of custom ornaments inspired by Quince's holiday world of cashmere and gingerbread, was illuminated as a flurry of snow fell, creating a magical winter scene. Thousands gathered last night at Toronto’s Distillery Historic District for the annual tree lighting ceremony and official opening of The Distillery Winter Village, presented by Quince. The spectacular lighting of the 55-foot-tall silver fir, adorned with more than 80,000 white lights and hundreds of custom ornaments, marked the start of the holiday season at one of the world’s most celebrated Christmas markets. The Distillery Winter Village runs through January 3, 2027. The tree lighting ceremony was followed by a performance from JUNO Award-winning Canadian singer Holly Cole. Now in its 17th season, The Distillery Winter Village runs through January 3, 2027, welcoming global visitors for seven weeks of holiday entertainment, shopping, food and seasonal experiences. All profits from opening night ticket sales support The Distillery Winter Village's local charity partners: The Anishnawbe Health Foundation, Soulpepper Theatre, and the Toronto Star Santa Claus Fund. Watch a replay of the countdown of the Christmas tree lighting ceremony on YouTube. "There's something really special about opening night, as the city comes together for the countdown and the Christmas tree lights up for the first time," said Rik Ocvirk, Vice President, The Distillery Restaurants Corp. and Director, Experiences & Events, The Distillery Historic District. "This year's tree is particularly beautiful, and our partners at Quince have helped us create something truly unique with all the wonderful details that visitors will enjoy seeing up close. After months of planning and preparation, it's incredibly rewarding to see The Distillery Winter Village come to life and welcome everyone back for another holiday season." Canada's Most Photographed Christmas Tree This year's Christmas tree is adorned with 80,000 white lights and 750 ornaments, featuring a family of whimsical 12-inch gingerbread characters dressed in miniature Quince cashmere sweaters, hats and scarves, 120 oversized custom-painted ornaments in matching Quince cashmere sweater colours with decorative icing details, and custom snowflake ornaments. At the base of the tree, three Quince gingerbread village vignettes come to life with animatronics in glass-fronted window displays. Gingerbread characters skate, ski, snowboard down a hill and ride a gondola, while gingerbread airplanes fly overhead. Large gingerbread houses complete the scenes, framed by a gingerbread-textured surround with three-dimensional icing details. Lanterns inspired by those found throughout The Distillery Historic District add a warm glow, tying the installation to its heritage surroundings. A custom-built circular platform surrounds the tree and includes a 3.6-metre (12-foot) performance stage. In total, more than 1,000 hours were dedicated to fabricating, detailing and decorating this year's Christmas Tree. Key Highlights for 2026 The 2026 Distillery Winter Village transforms Toronto's 13-acre pedestrian-only heritage district into a global holiday destination, expecting to attract a million visitors, and features live performances, immersive experiences, shopping, and more than 60 food and retail vendors and outdoor bars. The site is decorated with one million Christmas lights, tens of thousands of ornaments, and 2,000 pounds (907 kg) of fresh evergreen boughs. This year's highlights include: NEW: The Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone Photo Experience: The Distillery's cobblestone corridor transforms into a Hogwarts-inspired setting, where guests can snap a photo alongside the Hogwarts Express and a Platform 9¾-inspired luggage trolley, or choose their Hogwarts House and pose at an interactive selfie booth featuring custom House-themed photo frames. The experience celebrates the highly anticipated HBO Original series, Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, streaming December 25, only on Crave. NEW: The Immersive Nutcracker: Enter through the towering castle door on Gristmill Lane for this 360-degree holiday experience at The Fermenting Cellar, featuring floor-to-ceiling digital projections, larger-than-life Mouse King and The Nutcracker characters, festive photo ops, exclusive story-inspired food and drinks, and interactive games. Separate admission is required. Santa's Village at Soulpepper Theatre: A European Christmas department store-themed setting inspired by Soulpepper's production of Parfumerie, featuring Santa and his elves, a vintage-inspired letter-writing station, specialty hot chocolates and sweet treats. Storytime with the Elves takes place daily in the atrium. Caitie and Tobee from Super Simple are back for a one-time special performance on Sunday, November 15 at 3:00 p.m. under the tree. They'll kick off their Countdown to Christmas tour with a high-energy, interactive performance from one of the world's most beloved children's brands. Free to attend. Live festive performances: Toronto Mendelssohn Choir (November 22), Opera Atelier (November 29), Canadian Opera Company (December 4), Mirvish Productions (December 13), Myriad Ensemble (December 17) and Kente Claus (Christmas Eve) featuring steelpan drums. The McGregor Carollers perform daily through Christmas Eve. All performances are included with admission. The Quince Cashmere Cabin: An inviting gingerbread-inspired cabin offering a curated selection of Quince's signature cashmere accessories, including beanies, knit caps, gloves and scarves, alongside holiday-scented candles and other seasonal surprises. Visitors can purchase select holiday gifts from the cabin's walk-up retail window, and capture a festive photo from the dedicated photo moment. NEW: Visit Costa Rica's Chocolate Waterfall: A taste of the tropics comes to Gristmill Lane with a flowing chocolate waterfall inspired by Costa Rica's lush landscapes and cacao heritage, framed by tropical foliage, wildlife décor, and festive lights. Visitors can sample chocolate-drizzled pineapple and banana, snap a holiday photo and step through an augmented reality portal to explore Costa Rica's natural wonders. Chef's Lane Returns: Following a successful debut last year, Chef's Lane returns for 2026 with four new cabins, four acclaimed chefs and four one-of-a-kind, holiday-inspired dishes created exclusively for the Distillery Winter Village. This year's experience has a fresh new look. The four cabins are turned inward to create an intimate, speakeasy-style laneway, complete with overhead lighting and peek-through windows that invite guests to discover what's (and who's) cooking inside. Featured chefs include: Michael Angeloni, Afrim Pristine, Taylor Wells and Arush Vardhan Singh. New food vendors: Prince St. Pizza, Carousel Bakery, Sweet Crumble, Potato Bar, Peacock Bakehouse and Sando Man! join returning favourites including Stick Shift Robata's A5 Wagyu Sando, Cluny's torched s'mores hot chocolate (and new Biscoff hot chocolate), Scooped by Demetres' Monkey Bread and Spirit of York's Yorkie Burrito. Other options include Japan Taco, WuBaEats bao buns, poutine, pierogies, empanadas, roasted chestnuts, Swiss raclette, BBQ from Grinch's Grill, doughnuts, crème brûléed crêpes, and Basque cheesecake – and so much more. NEW: The Canuck Tavern: A love letter to the Great White North, this outdoor bar on the Archeo Patio celebrates Canadian pride with hockey, cottage-country charm and iconic Canadian landscapes. Enjoy Muskoka chairs around the fire, s'mores, hockey on the big screen, Canadian beer and spirits, and photo ops including a canoe against a hand-painted, Group of Seven-inspired mural, two oversized gondola chairs, a hockey penalty box and a giant topiary moose. Tributes to famous Canadians including Terry Fox, Roberta Bondar and Michael J. Fox, plus a message board where visitors can share what they love about Canada, round out the experience. NEW: Silent Nite Disco: The Cluny Tunnel features mirror balls, starburst lighting, giant disco ball-covered snow people and silent (headphone) DJ nights on the heated patio, alongside Parisian-style mousse au chocolat in cherry, espresso or Belgian chocolate flavours. Outdoor drinks: The Naughty or Nice Bar returns to the Pure Spirits Courtyard with a refreshed look, 50,000 white-and-blue lights, 300 hand-sewn icicles, and a long communal table. New on Trinity Street, Merry Matcha offers alcohol-free drinks in flavours including coconut, strawberry rose, lavender, ubé and vanilla. Holiday shopping: Support local and find unique gifts for everyone on your list at seasonal vendor cabins and more than 90 permanent businesses offering handmade jewellery, gourmet treats, home décor, original art, and self-care services. Ninety per cent of the permanent shops are Canadian-owned, and 30 per cent of merchandise is made on-site at The Distillery District by local makers. New this year, The Cooperage Marketplace brings together seven independent, founder-operated Canadian businesses, while the recently launched Maplee Market showcases local brands and independent makers. Holiday photo ops: The Christmas Tree, Countdown to Christmas Clock, Santa's Sleigh and Reindeer, Alley Press' vintage-style newspaper photo booth, Giant Snowpeople, LOVE, FAMILY, JOY and PEACE marquee signs, The Heart of Christmas, and The Quince Gingerbread Family interactive photo installation. Tickets and Planning Your Visit The Distillery Winter Village runs daily from Thursday, November 12, 2026 to Sunday, January 3, 2027, and is closed Christmas Day. Tickets are required during peak periods, including: Opening Night; Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays after 4:00 p.m.; Thursdays in December after 4:00 p.m.; and, Daily after 4:00 p.m. from December 14-31. Admission is free all day Monday to Wednesday through December 13, 2026, and every day before 4:00 p.m. Tickets start at $16, plus HST and service charge, with General Admission, Flex and Express ticket options available. Kids aged nine and under always enter free and do not require a ticket. For the complete ticket calendar, ticket options and everything visitors need to plan their trip including how to get here, visit TheDistilleryWinterVillage.com. ABOUT THE DISTILLERY WINTER VILLAGE The Distillery Winter Village is Toronto's original outdoor Christmas market, set within The Distillery Historic District. Recognized among the best Christmas markets in the world, it welcomes more than one million visitors each year from across Canada and around the world. For seven weeks each winter, the pedestrian-only neighbourhood transforms into a festive destination featuring its famous centrepiece Christmas tree, seasonal vendor cabins, holiday performances and themed food and beverage experiences. The event employs more than 700 seasonal workers and raises funds for local charities. For more information and tickets, visit TheDistilleryWinterVillage.com. ABOUT QUINCE Quince is a manufacturer-to-consumer platform offering a curated assortment of the world's best-made essentials, from cashmere and linen to fine jewelry and furniture, across more than 100 categories. By connecting shoppers directly to the manufacturing partners who make each product, Quince prices its assortment 50 to 70 percent below comparable market prices without compromising on quality, backed by a 365-day return policy and a 4.7 average customer rating across millions of reviews. Founded in January 2019 by three co-founders and headquartered in San Francisco, Quince closed its Series E in March 2026 at a $10.1 billion valuation and is one of the fastest-growing private companies in the country. Explore the full Canadian experience at Quince.ca, or download the Quince app on the App Store and the Google Play Store, with free shipping, free 365-day returns, and all prices in CAD including duties. sa.title: بمشاركة أكثر من 60 فنانًا سعوديًا وباكستانيًا.. معرض «واحد» يجمع الثقافتين في جدة
sa.description: افتتحت القنصلية العامة لجمهورية باكستان الإسلامية بجدة معرض الفنون التشكيلية السعودي الباكستاني «واحد»، تحت شعار «روح واحدة وتراث مشترك وتعبيرات متنوعة»، بمشاركة أكثر من 60 فنانًا وفنانة من البلدين، وبحضور عدد من المسؤولين والدبلوماسيين والمثقفين والفنانين ورجال الأعمال.**media[2794076]**وشهد حفل الافتتاح مشاركة مدير الجمعية العربية السعودية للثقافة والفنون بجدة محمد آل صبيح ضيفَ شرف، حيث أكد في كلمته أهمية المعارض الفنية في إبراز المنجز الإبداعي وإتاحة مساحات للتفاعل بين الفنانين والجمهور، ودورها في إثراء المشهد الثقافي والفني، مشيرًا إلى أن الفنون البصرية تمثل لغة إنسانية تتجاوز الحدود الجغرافية، وتعزز الحوار والتواصل بين الثقافات، بما تحمله من قيم جمالية وتعبيرات تعكس تنوع التجارب الإنسانية.**media[2794071]**من جانبه، أكد القنصل العام الباكستاني بجدة مصطفى رباني عمق العلاقات الأخوية التي تجمع المملكة العربية السعودية وجمهورية باكستان الإسلامية، وما تستند إليه من روابط دينية وثقافية راسخة، مشيرًا إلى أن معرض «واحد» يجسد وحدة الروح والتقارب الإنساني بين الشعبين رغم اختلاف الهويات الوطنية، مثمنًا جهود الفنانين المشاركين ومنسقة المعرض الفنانة ماهرة علي في إنجاح هذه التظاهرة الفنية.**media[2794067]**وفي كلمته، أوضح المدير العام لفرع وزارة الإعلام بمنطقة مكة المكرمة عبدالخالق عبدالله الزهراني أن المعرض يعكس ثراء الثقافتين السعودية والباكستانية، ويؤكد أهمية الفنون في بناء جسور التواصل وتعزيز الحوار الثقافي من خلال لغة الجمال والإبداع.**media[2794074]**ويضم المعرض مجموعة متنوعة من الأعمال التشكيلية وفنون الخط العربي، من بينها أعمال لسفير باكستان لدى المملكة أحمد فاروق، والخطاط العالمي شفيق الزمان، إلى جانب إبداعات فنانين سعوديين وباكستانيين تنوعت في أساليبها ومدارسها الفنية، وعكست خصوصية التجارب الإبداعية وثراء الموروث الثقافي للبلدين.**media[2794075]**وشهد المعرض حضورًا لافتًا لأعضاء السلك الدبلوماسي وعدد من المسؤولين والمثقفين والفنانين والمهتمين بالفنون البصرية، في تظاهرة ثقافية وفنية عكست عمق العلاقات السعودية الباكستانية، وأكدت دور الفن في تعزيز التواصل الإنساني والحوار بين الثقافات.

sa.title: «التعليم»: 30 طالبًا الحد الأعلى لفصول الدمج الكلي و3 طلاب لفصول الصم المكفوفين
sa.description: حددت وزارة التعليم 30 طالبًا حدًا أقصى للطاقة الاستيعابية لفصول الدمج الكلي في المراحل الابتدائية والمتوسطة والثانوية، على ألا تتجاوز نسبة الطلاب ذوي الإعاقة 25% من إجمالي طلاب التعليم العام في الفصل، فيما خفضت الطاقة الاستيعابية للفصول الخاصة وفق طبيعة الإعاقة، لتصل إلى 3 طلاب فقط في الفصول المخصصة للصم المكفوفين. وأوضح الدليل التنظيمي لبرامج ذوي الإعاقة أن تحديد أعداد الطلاب في الفصول الدراسية يخضع لضوابط تراعي نوع الإعاقة والاحتياجات التعليمية والخدمات المساندة، إلى جانب المساحة المعتمدة لكل طالب والطاقة الاستيعابية للفصل، بما يضمن توفير بيئة تعليمية مناسبة في رياض الأطفال ومراحل التعليم العام. ونص الدليل على ألا يزيد عدد الطلاب ذوي الإعاقة السمعية «الصم» على 10 طلاب في الفصل الواحد بالفصول الخاصة المدمجة في مدارس التعليم العام والمعاهد، وينطبق العدد نفسه على الطلاب ذوي الإعاقة الفكرية في المراحل الابتدائية والمتوسطة والثانوية أو التأهيلية، مع التأكيد على عدم تسبب هذه الحدود العددية في إقصاء الطلاب أو وجود قوائم انتظار. 5 طلاب للتوحد وتعدد الإعاقة وفيما يتعلق بالطلاب ذوي اضطراب طيف التوحد من فئة الأداء المنخفض، حدد الدليل 5 طلاب حدًا أقصى للفصل الواحد في المعاهد والمراكز والفصول الخاصة الملحقة بمدارس التعليم العام، خلال مرحلة رياض الأطفال والمراحل الابتدائية والمتوسطة والتأهيلية. كما حدد العدد نفسه للفصول الخاصة بالطلاب ذوي تعدد الإعاقة، فيما خُفض الحد الأعلى إلى 3 طلاب في الفصول المخصصة لذوي الإعاقات الحسية المزدوجة «الصم المكفوفين»، مراعاة لاحتياجاتهم التعليمية والتأهيلية. تحديد المكان التعليمي وبيّن الدليل أن تحديد المكان التعليمي المناسب للطالب ذي الإعاقة يعتمد على قدراته واحتياجاته وخصائصه الفردية، من خلال خيارات تشمل فصول التعليم العام المدعومة بخدمات غرفة المصادر، أو الفصول الخاصة الملحقة بالمدارس، أو المعاهد والمراكز المتخصصة، مع مراعاة توفير البيئة التعليمية الأقل تقييدًا وتحقيق متطلبات الوصول الشامل. وأكد أن الطلاب ذوي الإعاقة في فصول الدمج الكلي يدرسون مناهج التعليم العام، مع إجراء التكييفات والتعديلات المناسبة وفق البرنامج التعليمي الفردي والخطة التعليمية الفردية، بما يتوافق مع قدرات الطالب واحتياجاته. ويشمل تطبيق مناهج التعليم العام الطلاب الصم في فصول الدمج المكاني والمعاهد، والطلاب المكفوفين في المدارس والمعاهد، مع توفير الوسائل التعليمية والخدمات المساندة المناسبة. خدمات لضعاف السمع والمكفوفين وأتاح الدليل التحاق الطلاب ضعاف السمع وزارعي القوقعة بفصول التعليم العام متى سمحت حالاتهم بالاستفادة من البرنامج التعليمي، مع تقديم خدمات غرفة المصادر والدعم من معلمي التعليم العام والتربية الخاصة، فيما تُخصص الفصول الملحقة والمعاهد للحالات التي تتطلب خدمات تعليمية متخصصة. وبالنسبة للطلاب ذوي الإعاقة البصرية، تضمنت الخيارات الدمج الكلي وخدمات غرفة المصادر والمعاهد الخاصة بالمكفوفين، مع توفير التعليم بطريقة برايل في المواد التي تتطلب ذلك، ومنها العلوم والرياضيات والمهارات الرقمية واللغة الإنجليزية. وشدد الدليل على مراعاة التحاق الطلاب ذوي الإعاقة البصرية بالمدارس الأقرب إلى مساكنهم، بما يتفق مع مصلحتهم ومتطلبات الخدمات التعليمية المناسبة، إلى جانب تهيئة الفصول الدراسية للطلاب ذوي الإعاقات الجسمية والحركية في الدور الأرضي، وضمان ملاءمة البيئة المدرسية لاحتياجاتهم. التعليم عن بُعد للمنومين وشملت الضوابط الطلاب الذين يتعذر عليهم الانتظام في الحضور المدرسي لأسباب صحية، بمن فيهم المنومون في المستشفيات، حيث تتولى إدارة التعليم ترتيب تقديم الخدمات التعليمية والمساندة من خلال التعليم عن بُعد أو زيارة المستشفيات، وفق الأنظمة والإجراءات المعتمدة. وأكد الدليل أهمية المتابعة المستمرة لتقدم الطلاب ذوي الإعاقة ومدى ملاءمة البرامج التعليمية والخدمات المقدمة لهم، بمشاركة معلمي التعليم العام والتربية الخاصة والمختصين في الخدمات المساندة، لضمان توافق البرنامج والمكان التعليمي مع احتياجات كل طالب.

mg.title: COMMÉMORATION DE L’ARMISTICE - La France et Madagascar honorent leur histoire commune
mg.description: La cérémonie du 11 novembre a été marquée par un hommage aux soldats français et malgaches tombés durant la Grande Guerre. Cette commémoration a également été l’occasion de rappeler les liens historiques entre les deux pays. Un moment de rassemblement et de fraternité d’armes pour nos deux pays ». C’est ainsi que Jean-Marc Grosgurin, ambassadeur de France, qualifie la cérémonie de commémoration du 11 novembre 1918, qui est la date de la signature de l’armistice. L’acte qui mit fin à la 1re Guerre mondiale. Comme chaque année, une cérémonie pour commémorer l’armistice a été organisée à la stèle des anciens combattants, sur le lac Anosy, mercredi. S’en est suivie une réception à la résidence de France, à Ivandry. Cette année, l’accent a été mis sur l’histoire commune entre l’Hexagone et la Grande Île durant la Grande Guerre. Alors que Madagascar était encore une colonie française, trente-quatre mille Malgaches ont été envoyés au front pour combattre en Europe. « Près de deux mille cinq cents ont été reconnus morts pour la France. Morts pour défendre un territoire qu’ils foulaient, pour la plupart, pour la première fois. Ils se sont battus pour des valeurs universelles : la dignité humaine, la liberté, la paix», déclare le diplomate français. La cérémonie d’hommage a également eu une dimension contemporaine. L’ambassadeur en a profité pour rappeler les valeurs de la paix dans le contexte des tensions géopolitiques et des conflits armés actuels. « Le 11 novembre demeure une date emblématique. Une journée nationale de commémoration de la victoire, certes, mais aussi, et surtout, de la Paix. Un mot qui prend aujourd’hui une résonance particulière en ces temps particulièrement troublés et incertains », indique l’ambassadeur de France, en ajoutant: « Aujourd’hui en Europe, au Proche et Moyen-Orient, en Asie, en Amérique, en Afrique, les tensions géopolitiques, les violences sociales et les conflits armés ont pris une nouvelle ampleur ». Construire un monde meilleur Le diplomate note que « la désinhibition de la force par rapport au droit, à présent omniprésente, menace plusieurs régions du globe et nul ne peut s’estimer à l’abri ». Il fait ainsi le rapprochement avec l’enjeu de la cérémonie de commémoration. « Dans ce contexte, il est plus que jamais essentiel de continuer à se souvenir, à entretenir la mémoire des conflits passés et de leurs conséquences dévastatrices afin de construire des sociétés et des relations internationales plus apaisées, plus justes et plus harmonieuses. Il incombe désormais aux nouvelles générations de relever ce défi », affirme-t-il. La transmission de cette histoire commune aux jeunes générations a ainsi occupé une place importante dans la cérémonie. Des élèves du lycée français de Tananarive, du lycée Rabearivelo et du collège de France et du Monde y ont participé, notamment lors d’une séquence mémorielle au monument de l’Ange noir, à Anosy. S’adressant aux jeunes, le représentant français les a invités à s’approprier cet héritage et à faire vivre la mémoire des conflits passés. Un appel à préserver le souvenir des sacrifices consentis et à contribuer à la construction d’un monde plus pacifique. « C’est maintenant à vous, chers jeunes, chers élèves, de vous approprier cette mémoire et de la faire vivre. Pour que le monde n’oublie pas. Pour qu’il ne répète pas les erreurs du passé et pour construire un monde meilleur, pacifié, plus juste et plus humain », soutient-il. Garry Fabrice Ranaivoson

mg.title: PATRIMOINE - Le Hiragasy reprend ses quartiers à Ampefiloha
mg.description: Après plusieurs mois de tournées, le Hiragasy fait son grand retour sur la scène tananarivienne. Deux formations réputées se retrouveront ce dimanche au Kianja Rochel Rasamimanana, à Ampefiloha. Le Hiragasy renoue avec son public de la capitale. Après avoir animé les campagnes durant la saison des famadihana (retournements des morts) et des kermesses rurales, cet art séculaire retrouve les amateurs tananariviens. Baptisée « Hiragasy Goavam-be », cette nouvelle affiche se tiendra ce dimanche à partir de 10 heures au Kianja Rochel Rasamimanana, à Ampefiloha. Pour cette reprise, deux troupes de renom se partageront la scène : Rafaralahy Raymond, originaire d’Ambatoantrano, et Razakason, venue de Fenoarivo. Leur confrontation promet une joute oratoire de haute volée, où chaque formation fera valoir sa signature et son savoir-faire pour captiver l’assistance. La troupe d’Ambatoantrano se démarque par des récits puisés dans le quotidien, traités avec un humour fin qui fait mouche auprès des spectateurs. Face à elle, la formation Razakason de Fenoarivo surfe sur une popularité grandissante ces dernières années, ce qui rehausse d’autant l’enjeu de ce duel scénique. Sauvegarde Au-delà de la compétition entre les deux troupes, l’événement mettra en lumière toute la richesse du Hiragasy. Cet art populaire repose sur une alchimie subtile mêlant chants, musique, danses et kabary (art oratoire), où les réparties ciselées et la gestuelle permettent aux mpiHiragasy de délivrer des messages de société tout en divertissant l’auditoire. Organisée sous l’égide de la Fédération des mpiHiragasy de Madagascar (FMGM), cette rencontre participe activement à la sauvegarde et au rayonnement de ce patrimoine vivant. Après une longue parenthèse provinciale, ce retour au Kianja d’Ampefiloha offre aux passionnés de la capitale l’occasion de vibrer à nouveau au rythme d’une tradition profondément ancrée dans l’âme malgache. Cassie Ramiandrasoa

mg.title: EXPOSITION - La Fondation H réunit plusieurs artistes pour ses dix ans
mg.description: Dix années de création, de rencontres et de découvertes artistiques. Pour marquer cet anniversaire, la Fondation H présente deux nouvelles expositions à Ambatomena. Entre mémoire collective, engagement social, identité culturelle et exploration des matières, les œuvres invitent à découvrir différentes lectures de la société malgache. La première exposition, intitulée « Prix Paritana : 10 ans de création contemporaine malgache », est placée sous le commissariat de N’Goné Fall. Elle réunit 21 lauréats et vice-lauréats de ce concours organisé par la Fondation H pour accompagner et promouvoir les artistes malgaches. Les œuvres, présentées notamment sous forme de séries, s’articulent autour de quatre grandes thématiques : le lien social, la transmission, la fracture et la résistance des femmes. Chaque artiste développe une approche personnelle en lien avec les sujets qui nourrissent sa démarche. Parmi les créations présentées, Viviane Rakotoarivony présente cinq photographies mettant en lumière la force des femmes à travers le portrait de Madame Justine, mère de six enfants. Malgré les difficultés quotidiennes, celle-ci conserve sa joie de vivre, illustrant l’importance de savourer chaque instant. De son côté, Rijasolo expose une série documentaire de 48 photographies en noir et blanc, réalisée entre 2013 et 2021 dans le Sud de Madagascar, notamment à Amboasary-Sud, Betroka et Menabe. Son travail retrace le phénomène des dahalo, les opérations de pacification et les interventions des gendarmes. « J’ai commencé par enquêter avant de suivre un capitaine et un régiment de gendarmerie. J’étais en pleine immersion », explique-t-il. Cette série lui a valu une distinction aux International Press Photo Awards en 2022. Avec son œuvre intitulée « Intervalle », l’artiste plasticien Andri Marcel donne une seconde vie aux tongs usagées et à divers matériaux récupérés. À travers ces assemblages, il questionne le fihavanana, la solidarité et les distances qui peuvent s’installer entre les individus. « Les espaces qui nous séparent rappellent aussi les liens que nous devons préserver entre nous », souligne-t-il. Il reconnaît également que le Prix Paritana lui a permis de mieux découvrir son identité artistique. Racines et mémoire Pour sa part, Dina Nomena Andriarimanjaka, artiste plasticienne et designer textile, questionne la place des femmes dans le récit de l’insurrection malgache de 1947. Au terme de douze années de recherches et de rencontres avec des historiennes, elle propose une installation immersive mêlant textiles, archives, broderies et silhouettes féminines. Le songosongo, plante épineuse, symbolise la résistance et la protection. « Les femmes étaient là, mais où sont les traces de leur participation et de leur engagement ? Mon travail cherche à leur redonner un espace de présence», explique-t-elle. La deuxième exposition, « Masoandro amam-bolana» (Du Soleil et de la Lune), est une exposition monographique consacrée à Temandrota, premier lauréat du Prix Paritana. Sous le commissariat de Tamsin Hong et Hobisoa Raininoro, l’exposition rassemble des créations réparties dans quatre salles et retrace les grandes orientations de son parcours artistique, nourri par ses origines du Sud, son vécu dans les territoires antandroy et sa connaissance d’autres régions, notamment le pays zafimaniry. L’artiste aborde des questions liées à la terre, à la mer, aux déplacements, à la vie communautaire et aux cycles de l’existence. Le titre fait référence au soleil et à la lune, mais aussi aux figures parentales, aux origines et à la transmission entre générations. Ses œuvres accordent une place importante aux matériaux naturels et recyclés tels que le bois, la sève, les fils électriques, les tongs, les perles, les claviers de téléphone ou encore les fragments de bois de pirogue. Parmi les pièces exposées, « Hazo manga » évoque la filiation et la continuité de la vie. Au centre de la composition, un élément en bois bleu symbolise les racines familiales et les personnes qui ont contribué à sa construction intellectuelle et spirituelle. Cassie Ramiandrasoa
